items.prompt: A university asks to make advising better. Three user groups, an email and spreadsheet workflow, protected records, and a backlog-reduction target are known. What should the architect produce before selecting a solution?
constraints: The current workflow and exceptions can be observed.
Backlog reduction needs a measurable outcome.

options.text: Start with one user group, pilot its current workflow, and use backlog and privacy results to shape requirements for the other groups.
Map the email and spreadsheet steps plus protected fields, then choose an agent whose pilot will discover user-group acceptance.
Write a structured problem brief connecting each user group and workflow evidence to outcome, access, data, and acceptance criteria.
Compare public advising benchmarks and choose a model, then validate exceptions and backlog measurement against the selected design.

feedback.Reason: The problem is still underspecified, so discovery must connect user groups and workflow evidence to the outcome, data boundary, and measurable acceptance before solution choice.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic advises defining success criteria before prompt iteration and tying them to the application’s actual user needs; the problem brief structure is scenario reasoning.
Details.scenarioApplication: Document each group’s advising decision, current exception path, protected records, backlog measure, and acceptance test before comparing models or architectures.
Details.errorCorrection: Model ranking and a future-state diagram assume a solution, while a field list omits workflow ownership and success evidence; a post-demo definition is too late.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If users, workflow, target, and access rules were already documented and only a model migration remained, a solution comparison could be next.
Details.transfer: Resolve the problem, users, workflow, data boundary, and acceptance measure before choosing an AI solution.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A one-group pilot can supply evidence, but it leaves the other groups’ needs and exceptions unresolved before solution selection.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Mapping fields and steps without agreed outcomes lets the agent define acceptance during the pilot instead of clarifying the problem first.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A benchmark-led choice tests capability before the university has established its own workflow, exception, and backlog evidence.

items.prompt: A hospital asks for an agent to handle bed transfers. Nurses mean a recommendation or an automatic order, the manager cares about shift-change latency, and tools are already chosen. What should be resolved first?
constraints: The word “handle” hides authority and side-effect differences.
Exceptions and approvers are not yet explicit.
The chosen tools can still be revisited.

options.text: Observe transfers, distinguish recommendation from order authority, name approvers and exceptions, and set shift-change latency before tools.
Keep the selected tools for a read-only pilot, log nurse and manager decisions, and infer authority from recurring exception patterns.
Prototype automatic orders behind a rollback, measure transfer latency, and use observed exceptions to add approval checkpoints.
Tune prompt wording around “handle,” compare action consistency, and revisit the tool contract if the prototype remains ambiguous.

feedback.Reason: The unresolved word hides different authority and service contracts; those must be clarified before a tool can safely create an order.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends defining measurable, use-case-relevant criteria before iterating on prompts or implementation; authority and exception boundaries are scenario requirements.
Details.scenarioApplication: Observe the transfer workflow, document recommendation versus order semantics, name approvers and exception handling, and set a shift-change latency target before tool selection.
Details.errorCorrection: A fixed toolset or early automation makes a consequential assumption, and prompt wording cannot authorize an order or define an exception path.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If handle already meant a read-only recommendation with a named approver, tool discovery could focus on latency and integration fit.
Details.transfer: Resolve ambiguous authority and outcome contracts before choosing or enabling tools for a consequential workflow.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Observed patterns can reveal exceptions, but they do not authorize an order path or resolve who approves it.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: A rollback limits damage, but it still prototypes an account-changing action before the authority boundary is explicit.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Prompt consistency cannot establish clinical authority or the manager’s latency requirement.

items.prompt: A city benefits office mixes speed, reviewer workload, accessibility, and protected data in a one-week triage-pilot request; triage may recommend but not deny silently. Select TWO discovery controls.
constraints: Applicants, caseworkers, and appeals staff have different needs.
Representative interviews and an owned requirement record are feasible.
The pilot should remain bounded and reviewable.

options.text: Treat every requested feature as required and defer the appeals boundary until the pilot has usage data.
Interview applicants, caseworkers, and appeals staff and record measurable acceptance criteria for the pilot.
Choose the fastest model and use reviewer workload as the sole scope measure.
Let the prototype decide whether an accessibility or privacy request is material.
Record data and permission limits, non-silent-denial constraints, and an owner for each unresolved requirement.

feedback.Reason: Representative discovery supplies evidence for the bounded scope, while explicit data, denial, and ownership constraints keep the pilot reviewable.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic says criteria should be measurable and relevant to user needs, including privacy and other material dimensions; the interviews and ownership record are scenario controls.
Details.scenarioApplication: Interview all affected roles, record accessibility and workflow acceptance measures, preserve the no-silent-denial boundary, and assign unresolved requirements to named owners.
Details.errorCorrection: Feature accumulation, model speed, and prototype judgment skip affected users or make high-impact boundaries implicit.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If all groups shared one workflow and no denial or privacy boundary existed, a smaller pilot brief could omit representative appeals discovery.
Details.transfer: Scope pilots from representative user evidence and make data, permission, and high-impact decisions explicitly owned.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Deferring appeals leaves a high-impact decision path unowned.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Speed does not establish accessibility, privacy, or a useful pilot boundary.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A prototype should not decide the materiality of its own privacy or accessibility requirements.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.b: Representative interviews connect the pilot scope to affected users and measurable acceptance.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Explicit negative boundaries and requirement ownership prevent silent denial and unresolved obligations.

items.prompt: An internal FAQ assistant is moving to a public portal with non-native speakers, screen-reader users, tenfold peak traffic, and employee-only notes that must stay private. What discovery step is required?
constraints: Public users and owners differ from the internal audience.
Accessibility, privacy, and peak capacity changed.
The internal speed measure is not sufficient evidence.

options.text: Scale the internal latency target for peak traffic, retain internal tasks, and schedule an accessibility audit after the public release.
Publish the copied FAQ with data labels and a support contact, then measure public accessibility and peak load in production.
Keep internal criteria for the first release, add a disclaimer, and route accessibility issues to support while traffic is observed.
Re-interview public users and owners, map changed data and accessibility, model peak load, and define privacy, escalation, and service criteria.

feedback.Reason: The audience, data, accessibility, and traffic envelope changed, so inherited internal assumptions cannot establish external acceptance.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic treats task fidelity, privacy preservation, context utilization, and latency as use-case-specific dimensions measured against actual needs.
Details.scenarioApplication: Revisit public user tasks, screen-reader outcomes, employee-note access, peak load, escalation, and service thresholds before selecting the rollout design.
Details.errorCorrection: Scaling one latency number, copying content, or waiting for tickets does not test external usability or protect employee-only data.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the public portal had identical users, context, accessibility needs, and traffic contract, existing discovery evidence could carry forward.
Details.transfer: When context or audience changes, reopen discovery for the changed users, data boundaries, and operating envelope.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Scaling an internal target does not establish public accessibility, privacy, or the new workflow’s owner.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Labels and a support contact do not replace discovery of public tasks or protect employee notes under the new path.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Internal criteria plus post-launch tickets leave the public accessibility and privacy boundary untested.

items.prompt: A city benefits office receives conflicting requirements: the director wants automated eligibility, the legal owner requires zero silent denials and a human appeal, and operations wants 80% workload reduction. What should the architect resolve before solution choice?
constraints: A governance charter identifies the legal owner.
Each requirement can have an owner, consequence, acceptance test, and hardness classification.
Workload reduction is a target, while appeal and no-silent-denial protections may be floors.

options.text: Combine automation, appeal, and workload reduction in one weighted score and let pilot outcomes determine the preferred trade-off.
Optimize the 80% workload target first, then add a human appeal path if denial complaints exceed the pilot threshold.
Resolve authority, classify appeal and no-silent-denial as floors and workload reduction as target, and record the priority.
Ask operations to select the largest measurable benefit, then obtain legal sign-off after the architecture is chosen.

feedback.Reason: Authorized ownership determines which condition cannot be traded away; workload reduction is a target and cannot override required appeal and no-silent-denial protections.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends defining success criteria tied to actual user needs before prompt or solution iteration; hardness and priority classification are scenario governance.
Details.scenarioApplication: Record the legal owner’s authority, classify floors versus targets, define tests for appeal and denial behavior, and use that boundary to compare architectures.
Details.errorCorrection: Equal weighting, complaint-driven repair, and operations-only selection cannot authorize waiving a legal protection or distinguish negotiable from mandatory outcomes.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If the governance charter had already approved the priority order and appeal owner, the team could proceed to architecture options and acceptance tests.
Details.transfer: When requirements conflict, resolve authority and classify hard floors before optimizing softer targets.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: A weighted score can let the workload target offset the legal no-silent-denial requirement; authority and appeal need explicit priority before pilot optimization.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Deferring the appeal makes a required protection depend on observed harm instead of treating it as a floor.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Operations cannot waive the legal owner’s hard boundary, and late sign-off reverses the decision.

items.prompt: A discovery workshop produces a list of desired features, but no requirement is linked to an affected user, workflow observation, acceptance measure, or accountable owner. The sponsor asks for architecture selection immediately. Select TWO: Which discovery outputs should precede architecture selection?
constraints: Interview notes, workflow observations, feature requests, candidate measures, and stakeholder roles can be linked; several requests conflict on speed versus reviewability.

options.text: Build a traceability matrix linking each requirement to affected users, workflow evidence, outcome and nonfunctional measures, and authority.
Choose the familiar architecture from the feature list and collect owners and measures during implementation.
Prioritize the sponsor’s most popular features and let a prototype reveal which requirements are real.
Start with the fastest agent pilot and use its usage data to define the other groups’ needs afterward.
Assign an acceptance owner to each requirement and resolve speed-versus-reviewability conflicts before selecting a solution.

feedback.Reason: Build a traceability matrix linking each requirement to user/workflow evidence, outcome and nonfunctional measures, authority, and acceptance owner; resolve conflicts before selecting a solution. The decisive constraint is Feature inventory is not structured discovery until each requirement has evidence, an owner, and an acceptance implication; architecture choice before that mapping would convert unresolved preferences into design assumptions.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic advises defining success criteria before prompt iteration and tying them to the application's actual user needs. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Build a traceability matrix linking each requirement to user/workflow evidence, outcome and nonfunctional measures, authority, and acceptance owner; resolve conflicts before selecting a solution.
Details.errorCorrection: Implementation would harden unowned preferences and make later conflicts appear as technical rework rather than unresolved requirements. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If every requested feature already had an affected user, observed workflow, measurable acceptance, and owner, the existing structured discovery brief could feed architecture choice directly.
Details.transfer: Trace users, workflow, authority, outcomes, and acceptance ownership before turning feature requests into architecture.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: Implementation would harden unowned preferences and turn unresolved discovery into technical rework.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.c: Popularity and a later prototype do not establish workflow evidence, authority, or measurable acceptance.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: A fast pilot assumes the solution and leaves other groups’ requirements and privacy boundaries unresolved.

omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.a: Required control: Build a traceability matrix linking each requirement to affected users, workflow evidence, outcome and nonfunctional measures, and authority.
omittedCorrectElementExplanationsByOptio.e: Required control: Assign an acceptance owner to each requirement and resolve speed-versus-reviewability conflicts before selecting a solution.

items.prompt: Discovery has covered each affected role, observed the current workflow, resolved authority, and produced measurable acceptance criteria. New interview requests repeat already answered questions, and no high-impact unresolved requirement remains, but the team keeps discovery open without an exit decision. What should the team do now that discovery evidence is complete?
constraints: The discovery traceability matrix, interview coverage, workflow observations, authority decisions, acceptance measures, unresolved-question log, and lifecycle owner are available.

options.text: Continue interviews to collect additional suggestions before setting an evidence boundary or handing requirements to design.
Move to design immediately without recording that discovery is complete or preserving the unresolved-question log.
Close discovery with the evidence-backed brief, record residual questions and a trigger, hand requirements to design, and reopen only on new evidence.
Keep discovery open indefinitely so future suggestions cannot be rejected as late.

feedback.Reason: Close discovery with the evidence-backed brief, record residual questions and a revisit trigger, hand the bounded requirements to design, and reopen only if new evidence crosses the trigger. The decisive constraint is Once representative requirements and acceptance evidence are complete, discovery needs an owned exit decision; indefinite collection adds noise and delays design without changing the authorized problem brief.

Details.mechanismOrProperty: Anthropic recommends defining measurable, use-case-relevant criteria before iterating on prompts or implementation. The case-specific population, thresholds, roles, and authority limits are supplied by this scenario rather than by the provider documentation.
Details.scenarioApplication: Close discovery with the evidence-backed brief, record residual questions and a revisit trigger, hand the bounded requirements to design, and reopen only if new evidence crosses the trigger.
Details.errorCorrection: The first has no evidence boundary and adds noise; the second loses the completed authority and acceptance record that should govern design. The competing action therefore leaves the stated decision boundary unresolved.
Details.boundaryOrTradeoff: If a high-impact role, authority decision, or acceptance measure were still missing, discovery would remain open and the existing scoped-discovery path would apply.
Details.transfer: Close a discovery phase with evidence, ownership, residual uncertainty, and a trigger that tells the team when to reopen it.

wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.a: Collecting more suggestions before setting an exit boundary adds noise once representative requirements and acceptance evidence are complete.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.b: An undocumented handoff loses the authority and acceptance record that should govern design.
wrongOptionExplanationsByOptionId.d: Indefinite discovery has no owner-controlled exit and delays design without changing the authorized brief.
